summary.intent: Continue improving the monokl code-search tool: land the lint/typos and harness-fix PR, then implement 'hit-first' retrieval so search rows include matching-line snippets, done properly (test-first, recorded decisions checked, on a fresh stacked branch).
summary.outcome: PR #60 (harness fix, typos in lint) was opened after a retry. The snippet feature was implemented test-first on a stacked branch, with an 8-column output, README, changeset and decision-record updates, a new harness metric, and all checks passing (633 tests, 98.2% coverage). It was committed, but the trail/PR via Entire had not yet been created.

repo: Search output rows previously carried only location and signature; block `code` and `matched_lines` exist in core but the output layer dropped them, forcing a second file read by agents.
The original spec's output included `code` and `matchedLines`, so adding snippets restores spec intent.
The rg-compare harness had counted local variables and `.d.ts`-only declarations as misses; it now scores only top-level declarations and ignores `.d.ts`, with a 90% gate (currently 94.9%, 56/59).
Remaining real ranking misses are generic one-word queries: `refined` and `source` in zod, `config` in axios.
Output header strings are pinned in many tests and in cli.rs; changing the column shape requires updating them all, plus README examples generated from real output.
Snippet rule: the first line is omitted only when the signature column already shows it; variable rows (null signature) now show their matching first line.
The repo's PR flow is: just lint (now includes typos), doc-check, changesets, drift, machete, tests and a coverage gate, plus a decision-record log and a changeset per change.

code.finding: Holds the output projection and the new `snippet` function with `SNIPPET_LINE_CHARS`; the projection moved to 8 columns, and the budget test header was updated.
Harness extended with a metric checking whether the declaration line is already present in the output, so no second read is needed.

workflow: The `gh` wrapper opens PRs via a bot app whose token depends on an unlocked keychain (Secure Enclave OSStatus -25308 when locked); the user wants PRs opened with `entire trail create` and linked with `entire trail link`, saved as a memory rule.
Test-first discipline: confirm the new tests are red for the right reason before implementing, then inspect real output before updating pinned expectations.
Compare before/after by building a baseline binary from a temporary checkout and running the harness on both, then removing the checkout.
On macOS, `sed -i` needs the BSD form for bulk-updating pinned strings.

friction: The keychain was locked, so `gh pr create` failed with OSStatus -25308 and the PR could not be opened until a retry in the next session.
The PR was opened through the wrong route (`gh` bot app instead of Entire trails), and the user corrected it.
A background shell command from the previous session was stopped without a completion record.
The first snippet rule was wrong (it dropped the first line unconditionally), requiring a red test and a fix.
Changing the header broke many pinned test strings and three-plus CLI test expectations, which had to be updated by hand.
open_items: Create the trail/PR for the snippet branch via `entire trail create` (the commit is made but the trail is not yet created).
Three real ranking misses remain (`refined`, `source`, `config`), with declarations ranking 4th to 7th; ranking was intentionally left unchanged.
The full `just ci` was not run for the earlier lint/typos change.
